we present a data-driven deep learning approach to grasp synthesis for robotic grasping of previously unknown objects, that we evaluate the method regarding the force closure of the grasp and that the approach is able to generate high quality grasps in simulation and in real world experiments.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach can successfully be applied for the task of robotic grasping of novel objects in real-time.
the approach is a good starting point for a deep learning approach to grasping, but it is far from perfect and there is still much room for improvement.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method that can grasp unknown objects using depth images only and that is able to generalize to objects that are not part of its training data.
we have shown that DCNNs can successfully learn to predict grasp success for a wide range of objects, even if the objects have never been seen before.
our approach is able, for the first time, to learn the mapping between a depth image and a grasp pose, which allows for the grasping of unknown object instances in real-world experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DCNNs are able to generalize to novel objects and grasp them with high performance.
DCNNs can be used for grasping of unknown 3D objects with full 6D poses in a data-driven manner using depth images.
DCNNs are able to learn the mapping between depth images of objects and their graspable regions, even when the graspable regions are not visible in the images.
